title: Power and Attention
excerpt: A talk on AI and the totalitarian state, a campaign's marketing decision, and an academic paper on cultural imperialism.

sections.title: The Assigned Role
body: Best believe it was absolutely not an independent "leftist" shooter. There's no such thing as left or right. It's much much bigger than that.
Start paying attention before you get caught with your pants down. Stop watching Love Island.

It's religion, power, and business. It's NOT politics. Don't start with the same garbage that these groups want you to do every year when something big happens. Stop playing the role they want you to play.
It's NOT left or right. Don't be part of the distraction. It's the people vs those with real power and religious agendas.

sections.title: A Marketing Decision
body: If you're bored, read about how Kamala made the dumbest marketing decision ever, so dumb that could it even be ON PURPOSE???!!

So before I begin I will say I don't entertain myself with deciding who I wanna vote for or which candidate is the right choice even though I do value and truly consider what is right or wrong for a large country/system. This is for many reasons that I will not go into here because it's not the point. (The "politics" we see now is disgusting, it seems as if it's just a game of who can put their money in the right places and get the most attention.)
Anyways, my main objective here is to give you some food for thought. I could care less about encouraging you to vote for any one of the parties, cuz again not the point.

To begin: for context in my media Kamala Harris is portrayed as this fool who's only political strategy is to act relatable. I've seen too many hilarious montages of her saying the exact same collection of sentences in many different accents (depending on her crowd and where she was). Please look it up, it's actually pretty funny — she goes from Jamaican to ebonic to southern to latino and more.

Another funny example was when she recently was speaking in one of her rallies/speeches and a crowd member had yelled out "Jesus is Lord!", to where Kamala responds with "you're in the wrong rally!". She got serious backlash from this all over the media and was (as expected) painted as anti-christ and evil and all that. Now please note I'm not even saying this makes her anti-christ or whatever, I could care less because again current politics is a puppet show ruled by money and kept alive by the foolish who entertain themselves with it.
But what's hilarious about it is that NOT EVEN 3 DAYS AFTER she went and did a speech at a large/popular church.
So again, her iconic strategy on being relatable.
Okay, for our final piece of context:
I'm sure you guys have heard about the P Diddy situation. My entire media is drowned in P Diddy's arrest and case, and his alleged raping, trafficking, drugging, etc.

I'm sure you guys have also heard about the Beyoncé situation and how the P Diddy situation sparked an insane amount of attention and questions of the music industry, hollywood, and celebrities in general and exactly how many of them are allegedly involved in corrupt regimes.

Now, could someone please explain to me why Kamala Harris (considering the millions of dollars that she is investing into her campaign and the money invested into marketing, marketing teams, analytics, media strategies, etc) had Beyoncé speak in Kamala's rally when Beyoncé's name is so controversial in media right now. You're telling me that Kamala's marketing team thought it was a good idea to bring on such a shaky and controversial name onto her speech — and Usher was on too, another name that's been swept up in the same unproven media narrative around the P Diddy situation. Whether any of that turns out to be true is beside the point. What matters is that the narrative was everywhere, and a campaign chose to stand next to it anyway.

Beyoncé coming in seems like the most careless decision on behalf of Kamala's campaign. Because ONE: why should celebrities matter in politics, again just there to capture brain rotted, celebrity worshipping voters. And TWO: you're gonna bring on someone whose name is currently being talked about in connection with a huge hollywood scandal (whose name hasn't mattered for years in the media, only for music, so why now all of a sudden does Beyoncé matter enough for politics). Something incredibly slimy is occurring in our government or at least in Kamala's campaign.

In fact, this looks like such a horrible decision that I am inclined to think that there's something even bigger. That Kamala's candidacy is literally just a facade. Millions wasted to get people talking about politics?? Doesn't fully make sense tho, but what else.

I looked it up and saw people think that Beyoncé and affiliates of Diddy (billionaires) are now endorsing the hell out of Kamala's campaign to simply make sure everyone involved in the Diddy scandal is safe. But that seems too easy and foolish considering Beyoncé's name right now. There has to be more. And considering Kamala's embarrassing campaign strategy of being relatable, it's like she wants to lose horribly.
